title: Lower-stack source identity is not preserved at the application boundary.
text: Some packet-level disturbances are absorbed; different lower-stack conditions can produce the same visible timeliness or availability fault. The mapping study contains 3,780 fixture executions.
caveat: Fixture measurements are separate from MAS task outcomes.

title: MAS propagation and final task outcome are different variables.
text: Among 15,882 applied faults, 14,192 have a recorded MAS consequence and 12,735 fail the endpoint. The 1,457 successful runs with a recorded consequence demonstrate that propagation and endpoint failure differ.
caveat: B denotes a recorded handling response, not a verified recovery chain. The linked evidence subset contains successful runs with a recorded consequence.

title: Fault observability changes how the workflow handles evidence.
text: Fault observability can change evidence handling. Inspect archived malformed and valid-partial examples, and the silent stale-replay case in Fig. 4. A well-formed carrier may still violate the current task or evidence contract.
caveat: The malformed and partial links span the extension and common matrix and are illustrative, not the exact historical pair or a new paired test. The paper does not claim that incomplete evidence caused a wrong numeric answer. Fig. 4 concerns stale evidence for a different task.

title: Fault sensitivity follows the communication dependency disrupted by the injection position.
text: I2 request loss can prevent evidence generation; I4 handoff loss may leave existing evidence reachable on another path. Aggregate non-delivery failure is 89.5% at I2 and 73.3% at I4, a 16.2-point gap.
caveat: Fig. 5 uses the same task, model, Flat workflow and repetition. Its direct branch forwards pre-interception evidence; it does not reacquire an independent observation.

title: Cross-domain sensitivity is shaped by information dependency, recovery opportunity, and evaluation contract.
text: Clean-conditional loss ranges from 55.2% in Admin to 90.5% in Shopping. The paper discusses recoverable intermediate state, the role of the affected request, and task-specific evidence requirements.
caveat: Cross-domain profiles are descriptive, not paired causal effects. Admin lookup and aggregation cases illustrate later filtering opportunities; they do not prove a universal task-complexity ranking.

title: Fault tolerance depends on information-path diversity rather than hierarchy depth.
text: Flat fault success is 53.0%, versus 3.3% for Sequential and 3.2% for Hierarchical. In Fig. 7, both latter workflows accept the same corrupted top-two answer for a top-one search-term request.
caveat: The figure is one shared-failure case, not an explanation of every aggregate failure. An additional Supervisor does not add an independent information source; workflow roles and prompts also differ.

title: Model configuration affects fault tolerance but does not remove communication-fault sensitivity.
text: All three deployed configurations retain high clean-conditional loss: Flash 75.2%, Qwen3.8-27B 78.8%, and Qwen3.5-9B 84.4%. Their ordering varies by workload.
caveat: These are deployed configurations, not a controlled model-size ablation. SWE/TAC fault trials replay frozen evidence rather than rerun end-to-end repair. Individual cases do not reproduce the aggregate paired tests.

title: Execution-side and information-side protection address different failure surfaces.
text: Action-only protects non-delivery and duplicate delivery; Semantic-only protects valid-partial and identity-corruption evidence. Combined succeeds in all 180 tested fault runs; stale replay shows no incremental gain.
caveat: The main factorial study has 864 runs. Fig. 10 uses a separate earlier guarded-recheck pilot; its exact pair is not bundled here. The links below are explicitly main-study examples, not substitutes for that figure.

title: Not all redundancy provides the same fault tolerance.
text: Under identity corruption, single-path and copied-forwarding each fail all 15 runs; fresh observation succeeds in 15/15. An intact alternate edge can bypass a delivery fault, while copying already-corrupted evidence preserves its error.
caveat: Independent acquisition here means a fresh observation through a separate path; it still shares the Shopping backend. This is not a guarantee for arbitrary second observers.

title: The execution–information dependency split persists under repeated fault exposure.
text: In the finite-exposure study, Action-only and Combined succeed in 18/18 non-delivery runs; Semantic-only and Combined succeed in 18/18 identity-corruption runs.
caveat: A second exposure occurs only if follow-up communication reaches it. Two configured events do not establish tolerance of persistent faults.
